clues.text: Featuring zero inversions, this high-speed ride climbs to a height of 170 feet and reaches a top speed of 73 mph.
Manufactured by renowned Swiss firm B&M, this crowd-pleaser welcomed its very first riders in 1999.
Thrill-seekers can take a ride on this coaster in the state of Virginia.
This coaster made international headlines during an inaugural run when Italian model Fabio was struck in the face by a goose.
Its name refers to the mythological conveyance belonging to the Greek and Roman god of the sun, music, and healing.

evidence.quote: Apollo's Chariot is a steel roller coaster at the Busch Gardens Williamsburg amusement park in James City County, Virginia, United States.
During the ride's inaugural run, a 10-pound goose struck him in the face leaving his nose covered with blood.
This coaster is themed to the Greek and Roman god Apollo, who is the god of the sun, music, and healing.
